title: Mathematics: notable papers in the 5 October 2026 arXiv batch
global_caveat: This is an inferred editorial selection, not an official arXiv trending chart. The papers were newly announced, and no reliable paper-level citation or readership signal was available for this snapshot; no popularity ranking is claimed.

sections.title: Fractal dimension of critical Gaussian free field sign clusters
sections.abstract: In low-dimensional settings, the authors identify equivalent notions of macroscopic Gaussian-free-field sign clusters and prove that subsequential scaling limits in dimensions 3, 4 and 5 have Hausdorff and Minkowski dimensions 1 + d/2.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove macroscopic cluster equivalence on a large class of sufficiently low-dimensional transient weighted graphs and show the scaling-limit cluster dimensions equal 1 + d/2 for d=3,4,5.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Metric-graph sign clusters of the Gaussian free field; transient weighted graphs below the mean-field regime; small-mesh critical clusters on εZ^d for d=3,4,5.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract establishes properties of every subsequential scaling limit, not uniqueness or convergence of the full family of scaling limits.

sections.title: Quantitative Gowers uniformity of the primes in intervals of length X^{5/8+ε}
sections.abstract: The paper proves quantitative Gowers-norm bounds for the von Mangoldt function minus a Siegel-corrected model in short intervals of length at least X^{5/8+ε}, with quasipolynomial savings.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims the first quantitative Gowers bounds in this setting and an efficient non-abelian Type II inverse theorem; the abstract also describes a joint application with Florian Richter to infinitely many {x, x+y, xy} patterns in the shifted primes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Intervals (X, X+H] with H ≥ X^{5/8+ε}; norms are for the von Mangoldt function after subtracting a Siegel-corrected model.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is stated at the specified short-interval scale and for the corrected model; it is not an unrestricted uniformity result for arbitrary intervals.

sections.title: Simpson's closedness conjecture in arbitrary rank
sections.abstract: For a compact Riemann surface and a stable graded Higgs bundle, the author proves that Simpson's associated locus of flat bundles is Zariski closed in the de Rham moduli space, in arbitrary rank.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims the closedness conjecture by proving exactness of a determinant connection form and using it to control one-parameter degenerations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact Riemann surface; stable graded Higgs bundle; locus of flat bundles admitting the corresponding Simpson filtration.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a new preprint claim; the abstract's setting is the stated compact-curve and stable-bundle framework.

sections.title: Geometric triangle-free graphs of large chromatic number
sections.abstract: The paper gives geometric constructions of triangle-free and large-girth graphs with high chromatic number, including box-intersection graphs in three dimensions whose chromatic number is (log n)^{1-o(1)}.
sections.claimed_result: Among several constructions, the author obtains a triangle-free intersection graph of n boxes in R³ with independence number n(log n)^{-1+o(1)} and chromatic number (log n)^{1-o(1)}.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The headline bound concerns intersection graphs of boxes in R³; the paper also treats unit-distance graphs, line-intersection graphs, circle tangency graphs, and ordered graphs.
sections.unique_caveat: These are specific constructions and asymptotic bounds; the abstract does not settle the unrestricted extremal questions for all geometric graph classes.

sections.title: Counterexamples to the Strong Roberson Conjecture
sections.abstract: The author constructs connected graphs refuting the Strong Roberson Conjecture and its immersion analogue, with explicit infinite families including cubic bipartite examples.
sections.claimed_result: For certain connected excluded graphs H, homomorphism counts from graphs excluding H as a minor determine the number of homomorphisms from H to any target; analogous counterexamples are given for immersions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Homomorphism-count distinguishability for graph classes defined by excluding a fixed graph as a minor or immersion.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexamples concern the conjectures' stated minor- and immersion-closed settings; they do not imply failure of every homomorphism-count characterization.

sections.title: Limit law for Brownian cover time of the two dimensional torus
sections.abstract: For Brownian motion on the unit-area two-dimensional torus, the centered square root of the time to come within ε of every point converges to a randomly shifted Gumbel law as ε tends to zero.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim convergence in distribution of sqrt(C_ε) - m_ε to a randomly shifted Gumbel law for an explicit deterministic centering m_ε.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Brownian motion on the area-one flat two-dimensional torus; C_ε is the time to come within ε of every point; limit as ε→0.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is for this two-dimensional continuous-time torus cover observable; the abstract does not assert the same law in other geometries or dimensions.

sections.title: A Matsushima theorem, uniqueness and K-polystability for Kähler-Ricci shrinkers
sections.abstract: For noncompact smooth Kähler-Ricci shrinkers, the authors claim a Matsushima-type centralizer identity, uniqueness up to biholomorphism on a fixed complex manifold, and K-polystability of an associated polarized Fano fibration.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify the centralizer of the soliton field with the complexification of its Killing centralizer, prove the stated uniqueness, and establish K-polystability of the associated fibration.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Noncompact smooth Kähler-Ricci shrinkers; uniqueness is asserted on a fixed complex manifold.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not spell out the full technical hypotheses behind the associated polarized Fano fibration or uniqueness theorem; consult the paper for precise conditions.

sections.title: Hausdorff dimension for exactly approximable matrices
sections.abstract: For a non-increasing approximation function ψ and its lower order τψ, the authors give a Hausdorff-dimension formula for exactly ψ-approximable m×n matrices, including inhomogeneous shifts, when τψ>n/m.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim dim_H Exact_{m,n}(ψ,θ) = m(n−1) + (m+n)/(1+τψ) under the stated lower-order condition.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Non-increasing ψ:N→(0,∞), shift θ∈R^m, integers m,n≥1, and τψ>n/m.
sections.unique_caveat: The displayed formula is stated only above the threshold τψ>n/m; behavior at and below the boundary is not specified in the abstract.
